flexion.note: Arm elevation 0-180 deg = about 120 deg at the glenohumeral joint + 60 deg of scapular upward rotation (2:1 scapulohumeral rhythm). At the glenohumeral joint flexion is a spin of the humeral head in the glenoid.

abduction.note: Arm-trunk angle 10-180 deg = about 115 deg at the glenohumeral joint + 55 deg of scapular upward rotation (2:1 scapulohumeral rhythm). The head rolls up the glenoid while gliding down.

adduction.note: Adduction below the vertical is limited by the trunk; the head rolls down and glides up.

horizontal-abduction.note: Starts with the arm abducted to 90 deg; the arm sweeps backward in the horizontal plane.

horizontal-adduction.note: Starts with the arm abducted to 90 deg; the arm sweeps forward across the chest.

circumduction.note: A cone sweep combining flexion, abduction, extension and adduction in sequence; the humeral head rolls and spins on the glenoid.

pump-handle.note: Upper ribs (1-6) rotate about their neck axis (mostly transverse): the sternum rises and moves forward, increasing the AP diameter of the thorax.

bucket-handle.note: Lower ribs (7-10) rotate about an axis nearer anteroposterior: the lateral margin rises like a bucket handle, increasing the transverse diameter.

nutation.note: Real range is only 2-4 deg; drawn 4x so it can be seen. The sacral promontory moves forward and down.

counternutation.note: Real range is only 2-4 deg; drawn 4x so it can be seen. The promontory moves backward and up.

depression.note: Opening: the condyle first rotates (spins) in the lower joint space, then glides forward with the disc beneath the articular eminence.

protrusion.note: Both condyles glide forward with the discs in the upper joint space; no rotation.

lateral-excursion.note: Chin moves toward the working side: that condyle spins while the other (balancing) condyle glides forward and inward.
